—Abrupt though this may be.

The notion that exorcising evil spirits is a priest’s vocation is mistaken.

pages.ja:
神父とは神の教えを説くものであって、悪霊を払うものではない。
彼らの神は唯一絶対。至高にして全なるもの。完璧な世界を作り上げた聖霊だ。
それが自らの子である人を穢し、自らが創造した世界を汚す魔などを容認する道理がない。

pages.en:
A priest exists to preach the teachings of God, not to drive out evil spirits.

Their God is one and absolute. Supreme, all-encompassing. The Holy Spirit who fashioned a perfect world.

There can be no reason for Him to tolerate demons that corrupt His own children—humanity—and defile the world He created.

pages.ja:
だが確固として魔は存在し、人を堕とし地上を汚す。
在ってはならぬ物が神の世界を冒涜する。
その矛盾を、彼らはこう定義した。
即ち。人を脅かす魔ですら、主が構築した世界に必要な欠片、愛すべき被造物なのだと。

And yet demons undeniably exist. They corrupt humanity and befoul the earth.

Things that should not exist profane the world of God.

They defined that contradiction in this way.

Even the demons that threaten humanity are necessary fragments of the world the Lord constructed—beloved creatures of His making.

その教義で言えば、魔とは天の使いである。
人の善性を鍛えるものが聖ならば、人の悪性を鍛えるものが魔であるだけ。
ソレらは同じ天の御使い。
主の教えを説く神父に、これを撃滅する権利はない。

By that doctrine, demons too are messengers of Heaven.

If the sacred tempers the goodness in man, then the demonic merely tempers the evil in him.

They are messengers of the same Heaven.

A priest who preaches the Lord’s teachings has no right to destroy them.

繰り返すが確固として魔は存在し、人を堕とし地上を汚し、人智及ばぬ凄惨な悲劇喜劇を演出する。
時に天の計りは、人の子に天の無力さを錯覚させた。
人智及ばぬ魔の所業に、偉大なる主の奇跡を求めさせたのだ。

But.

To repeat: demons undeniably exist. They corrupt humanity, defile the earth, and stage tragedies and farces so hideous as to lie beyond all human understanding.

At times, the designs of Heaven made the children of man mistake Heaven itself for powerless.

Faced with demonic deeds beyond mortal comprehension, they sought miracles from their almighty Lord.

以って、ここに特例が生じた。
主の教えを説くのではなく、人の身でありながら主の代行を成す使徒が赦された。
本来傍観すべき試練、
本来否定すべき異端。
本来存在しない筈の第八秘跡を身につける者、
百二十の枢機卿によって立案された魔の撃滅者、『代行者』が誕生したのである。

pages.en:
Thus arose an exception.

Apostles were sanctioned who, rather than preach the Lord’s word, acted in His stead despite possessing mortal flesh.

Trials that should properly be observed.

Heresies that should properly be denied.

Those who mastered an Eighth Sacrament that should never have existed.

Thus the hundred and twenty cardinals devised their destroyers of demons: the Executors.

pages.ja:
彼らは魔を払い、主の教えに存在しないモノを排除する。
教義にないモノを狩りとる彼らは、教義に縛られる事もない。
結論から言えば、彼らには“不徳”が許される。
守るべきはただ一つ、偉大なる主の御名のみ。
その為ならば、主の被造物である魔すら滅ぼし尽くす。
彼らが悪魔払いと一線を画すのは、ただその一点のみである。

They cast out demons and eliminate things for which the Lord’s teachings make no provision.

Because they hunt what lies outside doctrine, doctrine itself does not bind them.

In short, they are permitted “immorality.”

There is only one thing they must protect: the glorious name of the Lord.

For that purpose, they will utterly destroy even demons that are themselves the Lord’s creations.

That one point alone is what separates them from exorcists.

The white skull sneers.

The priest—Kirei Kotomine—makes no reply as he checks his armaments.

Ten Black Keys—blades of confession—five to either side. Upon his right arm, several Command Spells left unused since the previous war and still retaining their power.

More than enough armament against lesser spirits.

Against a Servant, however, even if every one struck home, they would not be enough to finish the job.

Nameless though he may be, Assassin is still a Heroic Spirit.

Only a Scripture-class weapon, such as those said to be carried by chosen Executors, could destroy him completely.

“————”

The priest does not move.

Keeping his eyes fixed upon the skull concealed between the trees, he listens carefully to the sounds of the forest.

Leaves brushing together.

Breath beneath the mask.

The wet hiss of flesh slowly melting.

And the footfalls of the mad warrior receding into the distance.

“So you noticed my presence, Kirei!

“Knowing that much, why did you stop? The Kirei of old would have used the boy as bait if need be and made good his escape.

“Yet here you are, making yourself the decoy in an uncharacteristic display of virtue. Surely you have not let sentiment ensnare you!”

Only the laughter echoes through the forest.

The white skull wavers faintly.

The priest does not so much as twitch an eyebrow.

“—I had no intention of saving Shirou Emiya.

“I simply had business here.”

He throws the words at the unseen old mage without even a spark of murderous intent.

“Oh? Business with me?”

“Of course. Either way, neither Emiya nor I is likely to leave this forest. I know we will be killed soon enough.

“In that case—it is only natural that, before I die, I take what steps I can toward my own objective.”

“Hm…? Then you do not care what becomes of Illyasviel? You came here to save her, did you not?”

Three Black Keys rest in his left hand.

The blades spread into a fan as the priest watches the skull before him.

“Yes. What remains for me to do is either keep Illyasviel out of your hands—”

…The murderous intent disappears.

The white skull camouflages itself among the trees and vanishes completely.

His laughter rings out.

Knowing perfectly well that he cannot win, the clergyman whose art is merely to repel demons stands against the Angel of Death commanded by the old mage—

背後には振り向けない。
振り向いた瞬間、黒い壁が一面に広がっている気がして、生還しようという気が萎える。

pages.en:
I run through the forest with Illya in my arms.

I cannot look behind me.

I feel as though the instant I turn, a black wall will fill my entire vision and drain away whatever will I have left to make it out alive.

I cannot afford that.

If my resolve falters even slightly, it will catch us then and there.

It will catch us, and both Illya and I will be killed.

“——Ah, hah, agh, ah, ah…!”

“　　　　　　　　　　　”

pages.ja:

いくらイリヤが軽いといっても、人を一人抱えて走るのはそれだけで速度が落ちる。
くわえて森の足場は悪く、踏み出すごとに前に倒れそうになる。

My legs feel ready to tear off.

However light Illya may be, running while carrying another person inevitably slows me down.

On top of that, the forest floor is treacherous. Every stride threatens to pitch me forward.

“Ah—! Hah, ah, ah, hah…!”

“　　　　　　　　　　　　　!”

Faster. Faster. Faster. Faster.

If I do not run faster than this, it will catch us.

The presence behind me draws closer with every passing instant.

This is no time to be running at such a leisurely pace.

I have to go faster—run as fast as Kotomine and get away with Illya…!

My heart is going to rupture.

It hurts. I cannot breathe.

The muscles in my legs are on the verge of tearing, and my bones are screaming that they are about to snap at the hips.

It hurts.

How long have I been running now?

Since parting with Kotomine, I have carried Illya and charged blindly through the forest.

I passed five kilometers long ago.

My brain is too starved of oxygen to work; maybe I have run twice that.

At full speed, never once letting the pace drop, I have kept running with everything I have.

I have run flat out until my heart muscle is seizing and trying to stop, yet the presence behind me keeps swelling without mercy.

Illya is heavy.

Oxygen is heavy.

Both legs are heavy.

Death is heavy.

If it catches us, we die.

The nameless terror of knowing one blow will kill me bears down upon my back.

I kick my fading consciousness awake.

Run.

Think of nothing now. Run.

Who cares if my legs are about to tear off? Pointless worry. Deal with it when they do.

For now, all I have to do is run for the exit with everything I have.

Pump gasoline into your chest. Turn the key in the engine that cowardice is threatening to stall. Keep it in top gear. Rip out the brakes.

“Hah—ah, ah—!”

“　　　　　　　　　　　　　!”

Without consciously bringing any of it to mind, I pass through every stage at once, in an instant.

The whirlwind comes from the side.

Smashing the trees aside, our “pursuer” strikes at us from directly beside us—!

A single blow crushes my resistance.

The Black Key, reinforced to the hardness of diamond with every bit of magical energy I possess, buckles like heated candy.

The impact transmitted through the blade races up both arms and through my entire body, sinking in from the crown of my head to the tips of my toes.

Shirou Emiya is not permitted so much as to slow that monster down.

My body hangs in the air.

No—I am flying.

Like a thrown spear, I have been knocked away by that one blow and am about to sail dozens of meters.

At this rate, I may be sent all the way back to the castle.

That is how vast the difference in our strength is. Escape is hopeless.

If I keep flying like this and hit the ground, I will die.

The difference in strength is so overwhelming that I am on the verge of accepting it as an unavoidable fate, when—

My heart, already on the verge of bursting, swells still further and screams with blinding pain, as though a crack has split through it.

Black mud has eaten into his entire body, and even the wounds Saber inflicted upon him have been left untouched.

His priestly vestments have been slashed to ribbons.

His ragged breathing will not settle, and his only remaining weapons are three Black Keys.

Unlike his voluble Master, Assassin is silent.

To him, combat is work.

The daggers he aims at vital points are also instruments with which to measure his prey.

When the first dagger is defended, he measures the prey’s mobility.

With the second, he measures the rules governing the prey’s actions.

He keeps a distance of roughly seven meters.

Remaining always at a range only thrown weapons can cross, the assassin estimates his prey’s “abilities.”

He carves up its limbs, exhausts its body, and drives its heart to the verge of bursting.

To Assassin, the daggers are merely preparations for the true killing blow.

He uses them to measure his prey’s strength, guides the battle toward one absolute opportunity, and then brings down his demonic arm.

It is work—an ordinary routine that affords Assassin no pleasure whatsoever.

Assassin has used more than twenty daggers.

Though he uses them to measure his opponent’s skill, every dagger he casts is meant to kill.

The priest has weathered them all, made it through the forest, and reached this ruin.

Assassin had underestimated him for being human. The priest’s ability merits astonishment.

But that too ends here.

His strength to run exhausted, the priest can do nothing but lean against the wall and watch Assassin.

Three Black Keys remain concealed on his person.

The seven he fired like bullets were all evaded by Assassin and vanished somewhere beyond.

“Then the curtain falls. Grant him mercy, Assassin.”

The skull wavers.

Without so much as a windup, Assassin fires his daggers.

Their targets are the brow, the pancreas, and the diaphragm—three points struck at once.

The violet bolts leave his hand simultaneously, within a single breath, and the priest meets them with the Black Keys he holds.

There is a term for it: forced mate.

A move that guarantees the kill once played—a move that makes victory certain.

This throw is such a move.

The three attacks upon his vital points are merely bait.

The instant Kirei Kotomine deflects the daggers will be his end.

The cursed long arm—the spear of a single wing—unfurls.

—It is an attack that cannot be evaded.

Assassin has grasped the limits of the priest’s body.

He knows the capabilities of his bleeding, exhausted prey.

The prey will defend himself from death by the daggers.

However much strength he may have conserved for a reversal, his body can no longer keep pace with the priest’s intentions.

After deflecting all three daggers, the only action left to the priest is a desperate leap straight sideways.

And barely four meters at that—nowhere near enough to escape this arm…!

—The demonic arm extends.

The priest feels no fear.

He had anticipated this development.

He knew the daggers were bait. He knew the demonic arm would strike the instant he deflected them. He knew that he had no means of evasion. He had read it all.

Therefore—

“I declare—”

The only course left to him is to stake this body on mutual destruction—!

But there is no problem.

Only Assassin’s demonic arm will strike true.

But regrettably, no matter what thaumaturgical effect the priest adds, his Black Keys cannot destroy Assassin.

The three blades will pierce Assassin and nail him to the trunk behind him.

But that is all.

The priest will achieve the feat of wounding Assassin—and in the same instant, his heart will be seized and his life extinguished…!

And yet the expected response never comes.

The man’s heart gives nothing back, as though it were utterly empty.

“————”

The priest’s black vestments whip around him.

He leaps.

The absurd ascent is like a shell fired from a cannon.

He releases muscles charged and drawn taut to their absolute limit, erasing ten meters in one superhuman bound.

High among the dense trees, his hand closes in an instant around the head of Zouken Matou, who had been savoring the priest’s execution.

His trusted guardian is crucified against a tree by three Black Keys.

To Assassin, they are no more than shallow wounds.

But they are sacred nails that make rescuing the old man impossible.

Had he not said from the very beginning that this alone was his objective?

Gripping the old man’s head in one hand, the priest plummets to the earth.
“Gih—!”

He walks.

Leaving a trail of blood across the wall, he starts forward with the same dispassionate calm.

pages.en: “Hahaha—hahahahaha! What an irredeemable man! Do you still seek the ordinary happiness of human beings? Had you not understood that such a thing could never exist for you!”

Tracks of blood, tracks of flesh, spread across the wall.

Only the old mage’s head remains.

His body has been rasped away against the wall itself.

Even the head is now less than half its former size.

With a wet crunch, his brain smeared into paste upon the wall, the old mage gives one final peal of laughter.

*“Eternal life is granted only in death.*

pages.en:
—The laughter fades.

An invisible weight, a form beyond the sight of human eyes, grows faint.

The Baptism Rite.

Of all the thaumaturgical foundations fixed into the world as systems, their Scripture—the “Teachings of God”—is held to be the greatest form of anti-spirit magecraft.

A key of Providence that returns to nothing those souls that leave the flesh yet wander on through the world, rotting into madness.

Thus, in an act of boundless mercy, it purified the obsession of the old mage who had lived for five hundred years.
